After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|WD=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''
昭和十六年　川南村にあった広大な{{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|lt=軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}}の牧場が落下傘部隊の降下場に転用され
同年九月から使用を始めた　翌十七年には兵営が建設され　数千の落下傘兵がこの地で
練武に励んだ。
天下る落下傘兵は　[[Tenson Kōrin|天孫降臨]]になぞらえて{{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|lt=空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}と称され　村人の庇護後援のもと精鋭
誇る空挺部隊が練成され　次々と南の決戦場に出て征き活躍した
しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|WD=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|WD=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|WD=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama City|1=Tateyama, Chiba}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]] . == See Also == * {{ill|10=ja|11=空の神兵|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} * Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Martial temple|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Martial temple|qq=}} and {{ill|Wen Wu temple|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wen Wu temple|qq=}} * {{ill|National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Eternal Spring Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eternal Spring Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Chinese [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:30, 25 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=File:川南護国神社.jpg |map_type              =Japan |type                  =''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrine|qq=}}''
(Formerly ''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokonsha|qq=}}'')|神社|name=川南護国神社|緯度度=32|緯度秒=42.2|緯度分=11|経度度=131|経度分=31|経度秒=34.6|deity=Approximately 630 Heroic Spirits from Kawaminami Village
12,000 Heroic Spirits of the Army Parachute Troops War Dead[http://miyazaki-sensokiroku.jp/modules/myalbum1/photo.php?lid=123 川南町] - 宮崎の戦争記録継承館（宮崎県 福祉保健部 指導監査・援護課）|alternative name=挺進神社|prefecture={{ill|Kawaminami|WD=Q964194|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}}|coordinates={{Coord|32.195055555555555|N|131.52627777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}} {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} (川南護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}}  {{ill|Japan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}}, or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this {{ill|WP:BLUE|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/WP:BLUE|qq=}} considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasukuni Shrine|qq=}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}} in 1939.{{Cite journal|last=TAKAYAMA|first=K. PETER|date=1990|title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081|journal=Journal of Church and State|volume=32|issue=3|pages=527–547|issn=0021-969X}}It is the paratrooper shrine '''Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine''' is a shrine located in {{ill|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|en|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|WD=Q964194|lt=Kawaminami Town|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}} , {{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|en|Koyu District, Miyazaki|WD=Q1132169|lt=Koyu|1=Koyu District, Miyazaki}} [[Miyazaki Prefecture|District, Miyazaki Prefecture]]. The temple grounds are also known as the birthplace of the Army {{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}. == overview == [[File:「空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地」碑.jpg|thumb|Monument to the "Birthplace of the Airborne Paratroopers"]] The shrine enshrines the spirits of 634 war dead from the former Kawaminami village and approximately 12,000 war dead from the Army Raiding Corps. This is because the Teishin Shrine, which was established within the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department, was burned down by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|en|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|WD=Q471889|lt=GHQ|1=Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers}} when it occupied Miyazaki after the war, and was therefore enshrined when the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was constructed. In addition, since the temple grounds are the former site of a landing strip for parachute training, a monument marking the birthplace of airborne parachute units has been erected there. Every year, an festival is held by the Memorial Association, attended by the town, surviving families, members of the Airborne Veterans Association and the Airborne Comrades Association, and members of the {{ill|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|en|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|WD=Q4596101|lt=1st Airborne Brigade|1=1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|WD=Q889751|lt=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force}}, the successor to the Army Volunteer Corps. Although it calls itself [[Gokoku Shrines|a Gokoku Shrine]], it is not included in the list of Gokoku Shrines across the country posted on {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=the Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}} website. (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|WD=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|WD=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|WD=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama City|1=Tateyama, Chiba}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]] . == See Also == * {{ill|10=ja|11=空の神兵|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} * [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:30, 25 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=File:川南護国神社.jpg |map_type              =Japan |type                  =''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrine|qq=}}''
(Formerly ''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokonsha|qq=}}'')|神社|name=川南護国神社|緯度度=32|緯度秒=42.2|緯度分=11|経度度=131|経度分=31|経度秒=34.6|deity=Approximately 630 Heroic Spirits from Kawaminami Village
12,000 Heroic Spirits of the Army Parachute Troops War Dead[http://miyazaki-sensokiroku.jp/modules/myalbum1/photo.php?lid=123 川南町] - 宮崎の戦争記録継承館（宮崎県 福祉保健部 指導監査・援護課）|alternative name=挺進神社|prefecture={{ill|Kawaminami|WD=Q964194|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}}|coordinates={{Coord|32.195055555555555|N|131.52627777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}} {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} (川南護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}}  {{ill|Japan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}}, or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this {{ill|WP:BLUE|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/WP:BLUE|qq=}} considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasukuni Shrine|qq=}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}} in 1939.{{Cite journal|last=TAKAYAMA|first=K. PETER|date=1990|title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081|journal=Journal of Church and State|volume=32|issue=3|pages=527–547|issn=0021-969X}}It is the paratrooper shrine '''Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine''' is a shrine located in {{ill|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|en|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|WD=Q964194|lt=Kawaminami Town|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}} , {{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|en|Koyu District, Miyazaki|WD=Q1132169|lt=Koyu|1=Koyu District, Miyazaki}} [[Miyazaki Prefecture|District, Miyazaki Prefecture]]. The temple grounds are also known as the birthplace of the Army {{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}. == overview == [[File:「空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地」碑.jpg|thumb|Monument to the "Birthplace of the Airborne Paratroopers"]] The shrine enshrines the spirits of 634 war dead from the former Kawaminami village and approximately 12,000 war dead from the Army Raiding Corps. This is because the Teishin Shrine, which was established within the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department, was burned down by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|en|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|WD=Q471889|lt=GHQ|1=Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers}} when it occupied Miyazaki after the war, and was therefore enshrined when the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was constructed. In addition, since the temple grounds are the former site of a landing strip for parachute training, a monument marking the birthplace of airborne parachute units has been erected there. Every year, an festival is held by the Memorial Association, attended by the town, surviving families, members of the Airborne Veterans Association and the Airborne Comrades Association, and members of the {{ill|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|en|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|WD=Q4596101|lt=1st Airborne Brigade|1=1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|WD=Q889751|lt=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force}}, the successor to the Army Volunteer Corps. Although it calls itself [[Gokoku Shrines|a Gokoku Shrine]], it is not included in the list of Gokoku Shrines across the country posted on {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=the Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}} website. (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|WD=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''

Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:30, 25 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=File:川南護国神社.jpg |map_type              =Japan |type                  =''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrine|qq=}}''
(Formerly ''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokonsha|qq=}}'')|神社|name=川南護国神社|緯度度=32|緯度秒=42.2|緯度分=11|経度度=131|経度分=31|経度秒=34.6|deity=Approximately 630 Heroic Spirits from Kawaminami Village
12,000 Heroic Spirits of the Army Parachute Troops War Dead[http://miyazaki-sensokiroku.jp/modules/myalbum1/photo.php?lid=123 川南町] - 宮崎の戦争記録継承館（宮崎県 福祉保健部 指導監査・援護課）|alternative name=挺進神社|prefecture={{ill|Kawaminami|WD=Q964194|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}}|coordinates={{Coord|32.195055555555555|N|131.52627777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}} {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} (川南護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}}  {{ill|Japan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}}, or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this {{ill|WP:BLUE|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/WP:BLUE|qq=}} considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasukuni Shrine|qq=}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}} in 1939.{{Cite journal|last=TAKAYAMA|first=K. PETER|date=1990|title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081|journal=Journal of Church and State|volume=32|issue=3|pages=527–547|issn=0021-969X}}It is the paratrooper shrine '''Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine''' is a shrine located in {{ill|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|en|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|WD=Q964194|lt=Kawaminami Town|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}} , {{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|en|Koyu District, Miyazaki|WD=Q1132169|lt=Koyu|1=Koyu District, Miyazaki}} [[Miyazaki Prefecture|District, Miyazaki Prefecture]]. The temple grounds are also known as the birthplace of the Army {{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}. == overview == [[File:「空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地」碑.jpg|thumb|Monument to the "Birthplace of the Airborne Paratroopers"]] The shrine enshrines the spirits of 634 war dead from the former Kawaminami village and approximately 12,000 war dead from the Army Raiding Corps. This is because the Teishin Shrine, which was established within the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department, was burned down by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|en|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|WD=Q471889|lt=GHQ|1=Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers}} when it occupied Miyazaki after the war, and was therefore enshrined when the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was constructed. In addition, since the temple grounds are the former site of a landing strip for parachute training, a monument marking the birthplace of airborne parachute units has been erected there. Every year, an festival is held by the Memorial Association, attended by the town, surviving families, members of the Airborne Veterans Association and the Airborne Comrades Association, and members of the {{ill|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|en|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|WD=Q4596101|lt=1st Airborne Brigade|1=1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|WD=Q889751|lt=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force}}, the successor to the Army Volunteer Corps. Although it calls itself [[Gokoku Shrines|a Gokoku Shrine]], it is not included in the list of Gokoku Shrines across the country posted on {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=the Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}} website. (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|WD=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''
昭和十六年　川南村にあった広大な{{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|lt=軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}}の牧場が落下傘部隊の降下場に転用され
同年九月から使用を始めた　翌十七年には兵営が建設され　数千の落下傘兵がこの地で
練武に励んだ。
天下る落下傘兵は　[[Tenson Kōrin|天孫降臨]]になぞらえて{{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|lt=空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}と称され　村人の庇護後援のもと精鋭
誇る空挺部隊が練成され　次々と南の決戦場に出て征き活躍した
しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|WD=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|WD=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|WD=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama City|1=Tateyama, Chiba}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]] . == See Also == * {{ill|10=ja|11=空の神兵|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} * [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[fr:Kawanami Gokoku-jinja]][[ja:川南護国神社]] [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 04:30, 25 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image=File:川南護国神社.jpg |map_type              =Japan |type                  =''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku shrine|qq=}}''
(Formerly ''{{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokonsha|qq=}}'')|神社|name=川南護国神社|緯度度=32|緯度秒=42.2|緯度分=11|経度度=131|経度分=31|経度秒=34.6|deity=Approximately 630 Heroic Spirits from Kawaminami Village
12,000 Heroic Spirits of the Army Parachute Troops War Dead[http://miyazaki-sensokiroku.jp/modules/myalbum1/photo.php?lid=123 川南町] - 宮崎の戦争記録継承館（宮崎県 福祉保健部 指導監査・援護課）|alternative name=挺進神社|prefecture={{ill|Kawaminami|WD=Q964194|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}}|coordinates={{Coord|32.195055555555555|N|131.52627777777778|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}}}} {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}} (川南護国神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}}  {{ill|Japan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}}, or a shrine dedicated to war dead.{{Efn|Is this {{ill|WP:BLUE|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/WP:BLUE|qq=}} considering that the shrine is literally named as such?}} Such shrines were made to serve to enshrine the war dead, and they were all considered "branches" of {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasukuni Shrine|qq=}}. They were renamed from {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}} in 1939.{{Cite journal|last=TAKAYAMA|first=K. PETER|date=1990|title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081|journal=Journal of Church and State|volume=32|issue=3|pages=527–547|issn=0021-969X}}It is the paratrooper shrine '''Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine''' is a shrine located in {{ill|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|en|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|WD=Q964194|lt=Kawaminami Town|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}} , {{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|en|Koyu District, Miyazaki|WD=Q1132169|lt=Koyu|1=Koyu District, Miyazaki}} [[Miyazaki Prefecture|District, Miyazaki Prefecture]]. The temple grounds are also known as the birthplace of the Army {{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}. == overview == [[File:「空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地」碑.jpg|thumb|Monument to the "Birthplace of the Airborne Paratroopers"]] The shrine enshrines the spirits of 634 war dead from the former Kawaminami village and approximately 12,000 war dead from the Army Raiding Corps. This is because the Teishin Shrine, which was established within the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department, was burned down by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|en|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|WD=Q471889|lt=GHQ|1=Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers}} when it occupied Miyazaki after the war, and was therefore enshrined when the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was constructed. In addition, since the temple grounds are the former site of a landing strip for parachute training, a monument marking the birthplace of airborne parachute units has been erected there. Every year, an festival is held by the Memorial Association, attended by the town, surviving families, members of the Airborne Veterans Association and the Airborne Comrades Association, and members of the {{ill|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|en|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|WD=Q4596101|lt=1st Airborne Brigade|1=1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|WD=Q889751|lt=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force}}, the successor to the Army Volunteer Corps. Although it calls itself [[Gokoku Shrines|a Gokoku Shrine]], it is not included in the list of Gokoku Shrines across the country posted on {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=the Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}} website. (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|WD=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''
昭和十六年　川南村にあった広大な{{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|lt=軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}}の牧場が落下傘部隊の降下場に転用され
同年九月から使用を始めた　翌十七年には兵営が建設され　数千の落下傘兵がこの地で
練武に励んだ。
天下る落下傘兵は　[[Tenson Kōrin|天孫降臨]]になぞらえて{{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|lt=空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}と称され　村人の庇護後援のもと精鋭
誇る空挺部隊が練成され　次々と南の決戦場に出て征き活躍した
しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|WD=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|WD=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|WD=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama City|1=Tateyama, Chiba}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]] . == See Also == * {{ill|10=ja|11=空の神兵|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} * They were renamed from {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|lt=Gokoku Shrines|lt=Shokonsha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gokoku Shrines|qq=}} in 1939.{{Cite journal|last=TAKAYAMA|first=K. PETER|date=1990|title=Enshrinement and Persistency of Japanese Religion|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23917081|journal=Journal of Church and State|volume=32|issue=3|pages=527–547|issn=0021-969X}}It is the paratrooper shrine '''Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine''' is a shrine located in {{ill|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|en|Kawaminami, Miyazaki|WD=Q964194|lt=Kawaminami Town|1=Kawaminami, Miyazaki}} , {{ill|Koyu District, Miyazaki|en|Koyu District, Miyazaki|WD=Q1132169|lt=Koyu|1=Koyu District, Miyazaki}} [[Miyazaki Prefecture|District, Miyazaki Prefecture]]. The temple grounds are also known as the birthplace of the Army {{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}. == overview == [[File:「空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地」碑.jpg|thumb|Monument to the "Birthplace of the Airborne Paratroopers"]] The shrine enshrines the spirits of 634 war dead from the former Kawaminami village and approximately 12,000 war dead from the Army Raiding Corps. This is because the Teishin Shrine, which was established within the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department, was burned down by the {{ill|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|en|Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|WD=Q471889|lt=GHQ|1=Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers}} when it occupied Miyazaki after the war, and was therefore enshrined when the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was constructed. In addition, since the temple grounds are the former site of a landing strip for parachute training, a monument marking the birthplace of airborne parachute units has been erected there. Every year, an festival is held by the Memorial Association, attended by the town, surviving families, members of the Airborne Veterans Association and the Airborne Comrades Association, and members of the {{ill|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|en|1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)|WD=Q4596101|lt=1st Airborne Brigade|1=1st Airborne Brigade (Japan)}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|WD=Q889751|lt=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Ground Self-Defense Force}}, the successor to the Army Volunteer Corps. Although it calls itself [[Gokoku Shrines|a Gokoku Shrine]], it is not included in the list of Gokoku Shrines across the country posted on {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=the Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}} website. (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|WD=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|WD=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''
昭和十六年　川南村にあった広大な{{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|lt=軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}}の牧場が落下傘部隊の降下場に転用され
同年九月から使用を始めた　翌十七年には兵営が建設され　数千の落下傘兵がこの地で
練武に励んだ。
天下る落下傘兵は　[[Tenson Kōrin|天孫降臨]]になぞらえて{{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|lt=空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}と称され　村人の庇護後援のもと精鋭
誇る空挺部隊が練成され　次々と南の決戦場に出て征き活躍した
しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|WD=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|WD=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|WD=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|WD=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama City|1=Tateyama, Chiba}}, [[Chiba Prefecture]] . == See Also == * {{ill|10=ja|11=空の神兵|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} * (See the section on Gokoku Shrine.) == History == {{main|Teishin Shudan|{{ill|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|qq=}}}} The following is a summary of the inscription on the "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment Monument" and references {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} With the establishment of the Army Airborne Training Department [[1941|in 1941]], the unit was relocated from {{ill|10=ja|11=白城子陸軍飛行学校|the Baicheng Army Flying School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in [[Manchuria]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=唐瀬原|Karasehara|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=新田原|Nyutabaru|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} in Miyazaki Prefecture. At that time, the Army {{ill|10=ja|11=軍馬補充部|Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Military Horse Replenishment Department|lt=Horse Replacement Department|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}'s military horse ranch in Karasehara, Kawaminami village, was converted and used as a parachute landing site. The assault troops were deployed to combat, and in order to commemorate the heroic spirits who died on the battlefield, '''the Assault Shrine''' was established on the grounds of the Army Volunteer Training Department in Toyohara in [[1944]] (Showa 19). 樺太の豊原（[[ユジノサハリンスク]]）でなく、川南町川南の旧地名。「豊原住宅」などにその名前が残っている。 In 1944, the '''{{ill|Teishin Shrine|ja|挺進神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teishin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 川南護国神社}}''' was established within the grounds of the {{ill|Airborne Parachute Unit|4=de|5=Fallschirmtruppe_(Kaiserlich_Japanisches_Heer)|10=ja|11=挺進連隊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Airborne Parachute Unit|qq=}} in Kawanami, Miyazaki Prefecture, to honor fallen soldiers. It was destroyed by GHQ after the war.{{Cite journal|author=Association to Honor the Spirits of the War Dead|year=1999|date=1999-3-31|title=Veterans Speak Out|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=Newsletter to Honor the Spirits|volume=34}} In 1949, it was enshrined at the newly established {{ill|Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|ja|川南護国神社|1=Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}. After Japan's defeat in the war, the building of the Army Volunteer Training Unit was used by {{ill|10=ja|11=宮崎師範学校|Miyazaki Normal School|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which managed the Teishin Shrine. However, the GHQ, which occupied Miyazaki at the end [[1945|of 1945]], burned down the shrine in the early summer of [[1946]] . For a time, the altar of Ishikawa Fujinosuke in Karase, Kawaminami village, was borrowed to enshrine the heroic spirits, but [[1949|in 1949]] (Showa 24), when Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine was built to enshrine 634 heroic spirits of Kawaminami village, the heroic spirits of Teishin Shrine were enshrined there together. [[1956|In 1956]], some of the heroic spirits from Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine were {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=enshrined|1=Bunrei}} at {{ill|Mount Kōya|en|Mount Kōya|qid=Q535065|lt=Mount Kōya|1=Mount Kōya}}. {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} [[1963|In 1963]], a monument commemorating the birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Regiment was erected. {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} [[1991|In 1991]], in order to leave a record of the volunteer corps for future generations, a monument was erected to commemorate “the origins of the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of the paratrooper corps at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine” {{Cite journal|last=英霊にこたえる会|date=1999-3-31|year=1999th year |title=一、老兵は訴える|url=http://www.eireinikotaerukai.com/pdf/tayori/Eireitayori_No34.pdf|journal=英霊にこたえる会たより|volume=34}} {{Cite web|title=川南護國神社|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~un3k-mn/gokoku-kawanami.htm|access-date=2019-12-19|publisher=愛國顕彰ホームページ|和書}} . == Monuments == === "Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps" Monument === {{Quote frame|'''空挺落下傘部隊発祥之地'''
花負いて　空射ち征かん　雲染めん　屍悔なく　兵等散るなり
昭和三十八年五月建立　　空挺戦友会　空挺同志会　遺族一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Birthplace of the Airborne Parachute Corps'''
Carrying flowers, shooting through the skies to advance, dyeing the clouds,
No regrets for their corpses, as soldiers scatter and fall.
Erected May, Showa 38 (1963) by the Paratrooper Comrades Association, Paratrooper Fellowship Association, and all bereaved families.|Inscription source}} === Monument commemorating the enshrinement of over 10,000 heroic spirits of airborne forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine === {{Quote frame|'''川南護國神社に空挺部隊一万有余の英霊合祀の由来'''
昭和十六年　川南村にあった広大な{{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|lt=軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}}の牧場が落下傘部隊の降下場に転用され
同年九月から使用を始めた　翌十七年には兵営が建設され　数千の落下傘兵がこの地で
練武に励んだ。
天下る落下傘兵は　[[Tenson Kōrin|天孫降臨]]になぞらえて{{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|lt=空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}と称され　村人の庇護後援のもと精鋭
誇る空挺部隊が練成され　次々と南の決戦場に出て征き活躍した
しかし　我々の悲願も空しく戦敗れ多くの戦友が戦野に屍を晒し　そのみ霊だけが当時豊原
にあった陸軍挺身練習部構内の挺身神社に神鎮り給もうたのである　ところが　二十一年初
夏の頃　宮崎県に進駐していた米軍は理不尽にも挺身神社を焼払ってしまった　拠り所を失
った英霊は　当時旧兵舎を校舎にしていた{{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|lt=宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}の寄宿舎周辺を　毎夜白い体操衣
袴姿で走り廻るという噂が立った。
そのようなことがあって　一時唐瀬の石川富士之助翁の仏壇にお祭りし　更に昭和二十四年
この護國神社が再建されるに及び　ここに合祀し今日に及んでいる。
護國神社の祭祀は　川南護國神社奉賛会によって永久に行われることに感謝し後世のため
ここに由来を刻しておく次第である。
平成二年十一月二十三日　　陸軍空挺部隊戦友一同|碑文引用References}} {{Quote frame|'''Origin of the Enshrinement of Over 10,000 Heroic Spirits of the Airborne Forces at Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine'''
In Showa 16 (1941), a vast pastureland of the {{ill|Military Horse Replenishment Department|ja|軍馬補充部|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Military Horse Replenishment Department|qq=}} in Kawaminami Village was repurposed as a drop zone for the paratrooper units.
It began use in September of that year, and by the following year, barracks were constructed,
and thousands of paratroopers trained rigorously on this site.
Paratroopers descending from the heavens were likened to {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|qid=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin|1=Tenson kōrin}}
and called {{ill|Divine Soldiers of the Sky|ja|空の神兵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Divine Soldiers of the Sky|qq=}}. With the support and protection of the villagers,
the elite paratrooper units honed their skills, deploying one after another to the decisive battlefields in the south,
where they distinguished themselves in action.
However, despite our fervent hopes, the war was lost, and many comrades fell in battle,
leaving only their spirits to be enshrined. These spirits were initially venerated
at the Teishin Shrine within the Army Paratroop Training Unit premises in Toyohara at the time.
Yet, around early summer of Showa 21 (1946), the occupying U.S. forces stationed in Miyazaki Prefecture
senselessly burned down Teishin Shrine, leaving the spirits without a resting place.
It was said that the spirits, clad in white training uniforms with hakama,
ran around the dormitory area of {{ill|Miyazaki Normal School|ja|宮崎師範学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Normal School|qq=}}, which used the old barracks as its campus at the time.
Consequently, the spirits were temporarily enshrined at the home altar of Fujinosuke Ishikawa of Karuse,
and later, with the reconstruction of this Gokoku Shrine in Showa 24 (1949),
they were enshrined here, where they rest to this day.
The rites of Gokoku Shrine are perpetually carried out by the Kawaminami Gokoku Shrine Supporters Association.
We express our gratitude for this eternal dedication and inscribe this origin here for future generations.
November 23, Heisei 2 (1990), from all comrades of the Army Airborne Forces.|Inscription source}} In addition to the memorial to the Army Volunteer Corps, a monument called the "Airborne Song Monument" was erected within {{ill|Nyutabaru Air Base|en|Nyutabaru Air Base|qid=Q3015913|lt=Nyutabaru Air Base|1=Nyutabaru Air Base}} of the Japan {{ill|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|en|Japan Air Self-Defense Force|qid=Q830305|lt=Japan Air Self-Defense Force|1=Japan Air Self-Defense Force}}, which is located on the site of the former Nyutabaru Airfield. Additionally, within the grounds of {{ill|10=ja|11=国立病院機構宮崎病院|the National Hospital Organization Miyazaki Hospital|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, there remains a war relic: the water tower of the 3rd Regiment Barracks. It is the only remaining structure of the military parade ground that was lost to farmland development, and it remains as a symbol of Kawaminami Town. Meanwhile, the navy also formed a parachute unit, and the "Nonochi Monument, Birthplace of the Navy Parachute Unit" was erected on the grounds of the Japan [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] 's {{ill|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|en|JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|qid=Q2901121|lt=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base|1=JMSDF Tateyama Air Base}} in {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama,
